app_documentation:
The Flower Delivery App is a multi-platform solution (web, iOS and Android) that lets customers order fresh flowers and bouquets online and follow them from preparation to the doorstep. Its main purpose is to make buying flowers quick and reliable. A first-time customer should be able to finish an order in under 3 minutes and no more than 5 checkout steps, with secure online payment and a chosen delivery date. The app is built with React (web), React Native (mobile), Node.js/Express (REST API), PostgreSQL, Stripe for payments and Firebase Cloud Messaging for push notifications.

The MVP covers five features. F1 Flower Catalog Browsing (High) lets customers browse by category, search by keyword and filter by price and color. Photos and prices are shown, and search results for in-stock items appear within 2 seconds. F2 Cart and Order Placement (High) covers adding items to a cart, choosing a delivery address, date and time slot, and paying through Stripe. An order is created only after successful payment. A declined payment creates no order and shows a clear error message. F3 Delivery Tracking (High) provides an order status timeline (placed, preparing, out for delivery, delivered), push notifications on each status change, and courier updates including Mark as Delivered, which records a delivery timestamp and closes the order. F4 User Accounts and Order History (Medium) covers registration, login, saved addresses, past orders with status and totals, and one-tap reorder. F5 Admin Catalog and Order Management (Medium) lets administrators add and edit flowers, prices and stock, with changes appearing in the catalog immediately. Admins also review new paid orders and assign them to couriers.

The intended users are three roles. Customers browse, order, pay, track deliveries and manage their accounts. Couriers see their assigned deliveries and update delivery status. Administrators manage inventory, pricing, incoming orders and courier assignment. The design uses a warm floral palette (rose primary #D6336C, sage secondary, Playfair Display headings with Inter body text), bottom tab navigation (Shop, Cart, Orders, Account) and six screens: Flower Catalog, Cart and Checkout, Order Tracking, Account, Order History and Admin Panel. It meets WCAG AA contrast and 44px touch targets.

Support expectations are driven by the non-functional requirements. Catalog and checkout pages should load in under 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users. All traffic uses HTTPS, passwords are hashed with bcrypt, and card data is handled only by Stripe (PCI DSS). Monthly uptime of 99.5% is targeted, especially around Valentine's Day and Mother's Day. Customer addresses and contact data are encrypted at rest and deleted within 30 days of an account deletion request. The data model has 18 PostgreSQL tables, including users, products, carts, orders, payments, deliveries, order_status_history and notifications. The delivery plan has 11 tasks (T1 to T11) from schema design to end-to-end QA and staging deployment. The main risks are scope across three platforms, Stripe webhook and order mismatches, FCM/APNs setup delays, peak-season load, and privacy compliance.
baseline_artifacts: Requirements_v1 (5 features F1-F5, technical and non-functional requirements, 3 user roles)
Design_v1 (6 screens, UI component library, color and typography tokens, accessibility and responsive guidelines)
Database_v1 (18-table PostgreSQL schema with encrypted personal fields and 30-day deletion support)
CyclePlan_v1 (Flower Delivery App MVP Plan, tasks T1-T11 and risk register)
SupportGovernance_v1 (app documentation, baseline list and glossary)

glossary.Order Status: The stage of an order in its lifecycle. Allowed values are paid, preparing, assigned, out_for_delivery, delivered and cancelled. Each change is recorded in order_status_history and triggers a customer notification.
glossary.Courier: A user with the courier role who receives assigned orders, updates delivery status and marks orders as delivered, which records the delivery timestamp.
glossary.Stripe PaymentIntent: The Stripe object that tracks a payment attempt. The app creates an order only after a confirmed successful payment (via webhook), and no card data is stored in the app's database.
glossary.FCM (Firebase Cloud Messaging): The push notification service used to alert customers and couriers about order status changes and delivery assignments, using device tokens stored per user.
glossary.Baseline: An approved, versioned snapshot of a project artifact (for example Requirements_v1, Design_v1 or Database_v1) that serves as the reference point for change control and support.
glossary.Account Deletion Purge: The privacy process that sets deletion_requested_at on a user and removes or anonymizes personal data within 30 days, while keeping anonymized orders for financial records.
